A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Discrete Copula Diffusion. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, proofs, and experimental appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original unconditional text generation, conditional text infilling, antibody infilling, and runtime results in Section 6, with implementation details and generated examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds runtime–perplexity and diversity evaluations of unconditional generation in Section 6.1 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The copula combination, approximate I-projection, and sampling procedures remain unchanged. Algorithm 2 explicitly documents the autoregressive unmasking variant already described in v1 Section 5.3 and Appendix E; it does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds longer-sequence unconditional generation at 1024 tokens alongside the existing 128-token evaluation. The WebText/OpenWebText setting, WikiText-103 infilling, and OAS antibody tasks otherwise retain their coverage.

E2.justification: MDLM, previously cited but not evaluated, joins SEDD-medium and GPT-2-small in the new unconditional generation comparisons in Figures 5 and 8. The SSD-LM text-infilling comparison and GPT/NOS-D antibody comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The additional unconditional experiments evaluate the existing autoregressive DCD variant, add sample-averaged token-frequency entropy as a diversity metric, and compare perplexity against runtime. The original experiments' sampling procedures, sample counts, MAUVE evaluation, and antibody settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds analyses of whether quality gains translate into runtime savings and how perplexity trades off against diversity at two sequence lengths. These extend v1's runtime-versus-step-count analysis, which is retained as Figure 7 rather than removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Existing sampling counts are retained; the new sentence-entropy average is an evaluation metric, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figures 5 and 8 add results for autoregressive DCD and its baselines on runtime, perplexity, and entropy, including MDLM and 1024-token generation. They report favorable quality–runtime tradeoffs and lower entropy than GPT-2. Original Figure 3, Table 1, antibody scores in Figure 6, and generated examples retain their results; the additions are not revisions of those same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A corrects Equation (11) from KL(p_theta || q) to KL(q || p_theta) and supplies intermediate steps connecting the optimal factorized denoiser to total correlation. Proposition 1's bound and the remaining theoretical results are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims remain dependency modeling through an inference-time copula, no required fine-tuning of the combined models, and comparable or better generation with 8–32 times fewer denoising steps. The abstract and introduction preserve this scope despite the revised conclusion and additional supporting experiments.

C2.justification: Section 7 explicitly discusses possible copula-model training requirements, approximate I-projection, and higher per-step cost that can limit speedups. Appendix F also interprets the newly measured perplexity–diversity tradeoff, acknowledging lower entropy than GPT-2.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository access link and Algorithm 2's explicit indexing and sampling pseudocode for the previously described autoregressive variant. Existing checkpoint links, training settings, masking details, and antibody hyperparameters are retained in the renumbered experimental appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shi et al. (2024), Zhao et al. (2024), and Guo et al. (2024). These expand the background on masked diffusion and continuous-time ELBO objectives and acknowledge concurrent energy-based copula modeling, without substantially redefining the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: Changes include localized explanatory edits, a rewritten concluding discussion, an additional experimental appendix, acknowledgements, and updated author affiliations and publication headers. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime–perplexity and entropy displays in Figures 5 and 8 and an Algorithm 2 block. The original runtime plot moves from Figure 5 to Figure 7, Algorithm 1 moves earlier, and sample figures are renumbered. The overall layout and original result displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens practical evaluation by examining runtime together with quality and diversity and adding MDLM as a comparator. It also corrects the KL direction in the central bound's proof, documents the existing efficient sampler, and states concrete limitations. These are useful, focused improvements in rigor and transparency around an unchanged method and retained original results.
